headline: The Fed is expected to hold in October; oil is still near $100
summary: Overnight, traders dropped bets on an October Fed rate hike (now 13.5%, down 14 pts) but still expect one in December (78.5%). Oil eased from last night's peak but is still pricing a strong chance of $100. Large bets went on the US–Iran ceasefire holding, diplomacy over Ukraine is fading fast, and money is moving from Anthropic to SpaceX in the IPO race.

takeaways.lead: The Fed is now expected to hold in October.
takeaways.text: No change at the Oct 29 meeting is 86.5%, up 15 pts in a day ($43M market). Large traders added about $57k to 'no change'. A December hike is still 78.5%, so this is a delay, not a turn toward cuts.

takeaways.lead: Oil cooled off a bit, but $100 is still the base case.
takeaways.text: WTI hitting $100 this month is 62%, down from 70% last night but still up 18 pts on the day. Military action against the Saudi East-West pipeline by Oct 31 fell 10 pts to 28.5% (thin $126k market).

takeaways.lead: Large bets say the ceasefire holds for now.
takeaways.text: About $100k of large bets went on the US–Iran ceasefire lasting through Oct 16, Oct 31 and beyond. Through Oct 18 rose 6 pts to 96%, and through the Nov 3 midterms is 77.5%. The blockade stays, though: it ending by Oct 31 is only 5.5%.

takeaways.lead: SpaceX is overtaking Anthropic in the IPO race.
takeaways.text: SpaceX as 2026's largest IPO is 64%, up 13 pts today and 21 this week. Anthropic fell 9 pts to 37%. Musk momentum is spilling over: a new market on the Tesla Roadster doing 0–60 mph in under 1 second jumped 76 pts to 95.5%, and about $190k of large bets went on the Roadster 'flying'.

takeaways.lead: Netanyahu's party is sliding before the Oct 27 vote.
takeaways.text: Likud winning the most seats is down to 31.5% (down 19 pts this week). Yashar is at 67.5%. Eizenkot is the favorite for prime minister at 47%, and Netanyahu is at 30.5%.

takeaways.lead: Golf: a LIV shutdown is now a coin flip.
takeaways.text: LIV Golf announcing a shutdown in 2026 jumped 14 pts today to 48%. It's a thin market ($77k), so treat it as a rumor signal, not a fact.

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: October US inflation (CPI) at 3.7% year-over-year is now 88.5% likely (up 32 pts; thin $12k market). The report is out Nov 11.
Hopes for Russia–Ukraine peace talks are fading fast: talks by Dec 31 fell 24 pts this week to 39%, and by Nov 30 fell 24 pts to 24.5%.
Press Secretary Katie Zacharia out by year-end: 38.5% (up 12 pts in a day; new $332k market).

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Rates: October Fed hike 13.5% (down 14 pts in a day), December hike 78.5%. Two hikes in total for 2026 is the most likely outcome (67.5%).
Bonds: odds of the 10-year Treasury yield hitting 5.4% this year collapsed from ~66% to 37.5% over the week, so markets see yields near a peak.
Oil: WTI $100 in October 62% (up 30 pts this week); $85 only 20% (down 43 this week). Hormuz traffic back to normal by year-end: 11.5%.
Largest company at year-end: Nvidia 69.5% (up 5 pts today), Apple 29% (down 5 today, still up 19 this week).
Gold reaching $5,000 by year-end fell 8 pts to 13%. The appetite for safe havens is cooling.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: Israel–Iran ceasefire through Nov 30: 57.5% (down 5 pts today). The ceasefire is fine in the short term, but the odds fade further out.
US invades Iran before 2027: 15.5%. NATO–Russia military clash by year-end: 23.5% (down 2).
Houthis losing Perim Island (Red Sea) by Oct 31 fell 7 pts to 10.5%, so the Red Sea standoff looks set to continue.

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Brazil runoff (Oct 25): Bolsonaro 78%, Lula 21.5%. A Bolsonaro win by under 4 points is the most likely result (40.5%, up 18 this week). About $63k of large bets went against Lula today.
France 2027: Le Pen 46% to win (up 5 this week), 88.5% to make the runoff.
US midterms (Nov 3): Democrats take both chambers 62.5%. Large buys today: $51k on Democrats taking the House (91¢) and $48k on Democrats taking the Senate (64¢).

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Inflation is running hot: October CPI is priced at 3.7%, mostly because of energy. Expect gas to stay above $4.
Mortgage and loan rates: one more Fed hike is very likely by December, so variable-rate borrowing costs should edge up.
Recession odds are still low (about 7.5%), and markets see the economy as running hot rather than cooling.
